They finished the year with five wins and 11 losses, and did not qualify for the playoffs.  The Bengals, who were then owned by Mike Brown, the son of coach Paul Brown, now turned to the son of another coach to lead the team on the field when he hired assistant Dave Shula to assume the head coaching reins. Although he finished his career with the Chicago Bears, he was formerly a quarterback for the New York Jets, Cincinnati Bengals, New Orleans Saints, Baltimore Ravens, Arizona Cardinals and Philadelphia Eagles.  He was drafted in the sixth round of the 1992 NFL Draft by the Jets out of East Carolina University.  His only Pro Bowl appearance came with the Bengals, when he was selected for the AFC team. He was named a first-team All-American quarterback three straight years from 1934–1937 and was a consensus All-American quarterback in 1935 and 1936.
